why: No hyperscaler has cut 2027 plans, but the risk has shifted to politics: after the Democratic sweep, UBS says ~30% of expected 2028 US data-centre additions could be at risk from construction pauses, and Microsoft is reportedly tightening oversight of neocloud projects. Spending is still debt-funded, with free cash flow negative at three of the four biggest spenders. New on Tue: momentum for a US plan to block imports of Chinese data-centre equipment, which Amazon, Alphabet and Meta oppose.

Nvidia beat forecasts (Q3 revenue US$115.8bn, +103%; Q4 guided to ~US$130bn) but its shares fell 2.9% on Wednesday to US$150.96, the lowest close since June 2025, after rising about 3% before the open. The board says it won’t bring back Jensen Huang, and the WSJ reports an SEC disclosure probe. Good numbers no longer lifting the stock is a classic late-cycle sign. The chip index rose 0.3% on Tuesday; its 2026 gain has shrunk from ~106% in June to ~34%.

A 25 bp hike on 9 Dec is ~96% priced, with 69% odds of 50 bp of hikes by end-January. Wednesday’s October minutes showed almost all officials expect further hikes, and a couple are open to more than 25 bp in December; Governor Waller again floated a half-point move.

Oracle −3.4% on Tue and flat Wed, about 40% down in 2026, with ~US$108bn of debt and a bondholder lawsuit; its default protection is reported near 300 bp. CoreWeave −5% on Wed (−34% in 2026) while it prices a new term loan at a 7–7.5% yield; its CEO says it won’t borrow unsecured at current yields. No newer CoreWeave level since 1,268 bp (5 Nov).

Anthropic priced its IPO at US$83 a share, above its US$70–78 range, raising a record ~US$81bn at about a US$1.5tn valuation, the largest IPO ever. It starts trading on Nasdaq as ANT on Thu US time (early Fri Melbourne). Strong demand in a falling market shows appetite for AI is not exhausted, but the first-day trade is the real test. Separately, Nvidia reportedly cut a proposed OpenAI data-centre guarantee from US$250bn to ~US$105bn (unconfirmed). (Disclosure: Claude is made by Anthropic.)
Eased to 5.07% on Wed (5.11% Tue) as oil fell: a mild flight-to-safety signal, not a sharp fall, and yields are still near their highest since 2002.
WTI fell 3.0% to US$82.08 and Brent 2.4% to US$90.93 on Wed, Brent’s lowest since late August, as Hormuz flows recover. Lower oil eases the inflation pressure behind Fed hikes.
High-yield spread 323 bp on 13 Nov (320 bp on 12 Nov): broad credit is still calm. IMF: US bank loans to non-bank lenders rose 18% in 2026.

Wednesday was mixed rather than broad selling: the Dow fell 1.1% and the S&P 500 0.2%, but the Nasdaq rose 0.4% and small caps 0.5%. On Tue the S&P fell 1.0%, the Dow 1.6% and small caps 1.5%. Gold fell 3.5% to a one-year low and gold miners fell with it.
